t: CNC Toolpath Generator - Signature build-tool concept
title: CNC Toolpath Generator - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Creates machining paths for supported computer-controlled equipment.
description:
The Signature CNC Toolpath Generator exists to creates machining paths for supported computer-controlled equipment. It is one of the fundamental capabilities in the AI build-tool catalog: the set of tools, engines and disciplines an AI needs to design, engineer, generate, test and deliver things on demand. Where public tools each solve a slice of the problem, the Signature line defines the whole capability as a coherent framework with contracts between its parts.

Consider what happens without a disciplined CNC Toolpath Generator. CNC Toolpath Generator work degrades into folklore - tricks that work on one machine, steps remembered differently by every practitioner, failures nobody can reproduce. The Signature framework answers with determinism: declared inputs, explicit transformations, verified outputs, and an audit trail that explains every result. The pillars below are the machinery that makes that promise concrete.

This is a Signature-concept database: the framework it describes is the Signature line's own design, labeled as such throughout. The techniques and standards records cite real public knowledge; the pillars and drills are the Signature system's original construction. All of it ships with runnable demos, because in the Signature line a tool proves itself by running.

t: Signature Slicer - CNC Toolpath Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Slicer - CNC Toolpath Generator framework pillar
definition: The Slicer component of the Signature CNC Toolpath Generator framework, owning slicer. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature CNC Toolpath Generator framework, the Slicer owns the framework's slicer responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Slicer's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Slicer from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Creates machining paths for supported computer-controlled equipment.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Manufacturing and fabrication build needs CNC Toolpath Generator, so the framework invokes the Slicer on the the framework's slicer responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for CNC Toolpath Generator. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Miller - CNC Toolpath Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Miller - CNC Toolpath Generator framework pillar
definition: The Miller component of the Signature CNC Toolpath Generator framework, owning miller. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature CNC Toolpath Generator framework decomposes the capability (Creates machining paths for supported computer-controlled equipment.) into seven pillars, and the Miller is the one that owns the framework's miller responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a CNC Toolpath Generator result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Miller's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Miller's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

t: Signature Cutter - CNC Toolpath Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Cutter - CNC Toolpath Generator framework pillar
definition: The Cutter component of the Signature CNC Toolpath Generator framework, owning cutter. Signature concept.
description:
The Cutter is a load-bearing component of the Signature CNC Toolpath Generator framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's cutter responsibilities belongs to the Cutter, and the Cutter answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Cutter can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Cutter works like this. A build request arrives carrying the CNC Toolpath Generator charter (creates machining paths for supported computer-controlled equipment.). The Cutter reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for a small manufacturing job that needs CNC Toolpath Generator. The Cutter takes the request's cutter responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did.
